precepts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not; they are new every morning, great is Thy faithfulness.
precepts.point: Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful. Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
“Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.” Because he is merciful, we are still here: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”

Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed. When the sorrows of death compassed us and the pains of hell got hold on us, we called upon the name of the Lord, and his compassions did not fail; they are new every morning.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
precepts.point: What shall I render unto the Lord for all His benefits toward me? The apostle Paul answered that question.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
“What shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits toward me?” The apostle Paul answered that question: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.”

For the Lord dealing bountifully with us, delivering our soul from death, our eyes from tears and our feet from falling, what we render is ourselves: our bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable unto God. It is our reasonable service.

precepts.text: One of His benefits is that the Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve and has given us such deliverance.
precepts.point: What shall I render unto the Lord for all His benefits toward me? The apostle Paul answered that question.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
One of his benefits is this: “after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”.

The Most High has punished us less than our iniquities deserve and has given us such deliverance. When the psalm asks what shall I render unto the Lord for all his benefits, that is counted among them: he preserved the simple, we were brought low and he helped us, and he did not give us all that our evil deeds deserved.
